chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Sayf al-Tammarr said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I came to the Black Stone and found it crowded, so I did not meet anyone except one of our companions, and I asked him.' He said: 'It is necessary to kiss it (istilam).' He said: 'If you find it empty, [kiss it], otherwise, send greetings from a distance.'

key_terms.اِسْتِلاَمِهِ: Kissing it (specifically touching and kissing the Black Stone)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for kissing the Black Stone if it is too crowded to reach it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istilam* (kissing or touching) the Black Stone as a recommended act of reverence during Tawaf, while providing practical flexibility for worshippers in crowded conditions. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual precision with ease (*taysir*), ensuring that physical obstruction does not invalidate the spiritual intent of the circumambulation. The narration underscores the Stone's role as a symbolic focal point of divine connection rather than an object of worship itself.
